Abdominal external oblique muscle.insertion: Xiphoid process,outer lip of the iliac crest, pubic crest, pubic tubercle, linea alba, inguinal ligament, anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS)
Abdominal external oblique muscle.action: Flexion of the torso and contralateral rotation of torso

Abdominal internal oblique muscle.origin: Inguinal ligament, iliac crest and the lumbodorsal fascia
Abdominal internal oblique muscle.insertion: Linea alba, pectineal line of pubis (via conjoint tendon) and ribs 10-12.
Abdominal internal oblique muscle.action:
Bilateral: Compresses abdomen
Unilateral: Ipsilateral trunk rotation
Abdominal internal oblique muscle.nerve: Thoracoabdominal nn. (T7-T11), subcostal n. (T12), iliohypogastric n. (L1) and ilioinguinal n. (L1)

Abductor digiti minimi muscle of foot.action: Flexion and abduction of the fifth toe

Abductor hallucis muscle.origin: Medial process of calcaneal tuberosity, Plantar aponeurosis, Flexor retinaculum
Abductor hallucis muscle.insertion: Medial aspect of base of 1st phalanx of hallux

Adductor brevis muscle.origin: Anterior surface of the inferior ramus and body of the pubis
Adductor brevis muscle.insertion: The lesser trochanter and linea aspera of the femur

Adductor hallucis muscle.origin: Oblique head: proximal ends of middle 3 metatarsal bones; Transverse head: MTP ligaments of lateral 3 toes
Adductor hallucis muscle.insertion: Lateral side of base of first phalanx of the 1st toe; sesamoid apparatus

Adductor longus muscle.origin: Pubic body just below the pubic crest
Adductor longus muscle.action: Adduction of hip, flexion of hip joint

Adductor magnus muscle.insertion: Linea aspera and adductor tubercle of femur
Adductor magnus muscle.action:
Adduction of hip (both portions)
flexion of hip (adductor portion)
extension of hip (hamstring portion)
Adductor magnus muscle.nerve: Posterior branch of obturator nerve (adductor) and sciatic nerve (hamstring)

Adductor minimus muscle.action: Adduction and lateral rotation of thigh
Adductor minimus muscle.blood: Obturator artery and the medial circumflex femoral artery of the femoral artery

Anconeus muscle.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus proximally
Anconeus muscle.insertion: Lateral surface of the olecranon process of the ulna and the superior proximal part of the posterior ulna
Anconeus muscle.action: It is partly blended in with the triceps, which it assists in extension of the elbow. It also stabilizes the elbow during pronation and supination and pulls slack out of the elbow joint capsule during extension to prevent impingement.
Anconeus muscle.nerve: Radial nerve (C5, C6, C7, C8, and T1)
Anconeus muscle.blood: Deep brachial artery, recurrent interosseous artery

Biceps.origin:
Short head: coracoid process of the scapula.
Long head: supraglenoid tubercle
Biceps.insertion: Radial tuberosity and bicipital aponeurosis into deep fascia on medial part of forearm
Biceps.action:
Flexes elbow
flexes and abducts shoulder
supinates radioulnar joint in the forearm

Biceps femoris muscle.origin: Tuberosity of the ischium, linea aspera, femur
Biceps femoris muscle.insertion: The head of the fibula which articulates with the back of the lateral tibial condyle
Biceps femoris muscle.action: Flexes knee joint, laterally rotates knee joint (when knee is flexed), extends hip joint (long head only)
Biceps femoris muscle.nerve:
Long head: tibial nerve
short head: common fibular nerve
Biceps femoris muscle.blood: Deep femoral artery, perforating arteries; long head of biceps femoris: perforating branches from profunda femoris artery

Brachialis muscle.origin: Anterior surface of the humerus, particularly the distal half of this bone
Brachialis muscle.insertion: Coronoid process and the tuberosity of the ulna
Brachialis muscle.nerve: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5-C7) and radial nerve (C5, C6)

Brachioradialis.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus and the orbicular ligament of the radius
Brachioradialis.action: Flexion of elbow, supination and pronation of the radioulnar joint to 90°

Bucinator muscle.origin: From the alveolar processes of maxilla and mandible, buccinator crest and pterygomandibular raphe
Bucinator muscle.insertion: In the fibers of the orbicularis oris
Bucinator muscle.action: The buccinator compresses the cheeks against the teeth and is used in acts such as blowing. It is an assistant muscle of mastication (chewing) and in neonates it is used to suckle.
Bucinator muscle.nerve: Buccal branch of the facial nerve (VII cranial nerve)

Calcaneus.description: The calcaneus (from the Latin calcaneus or calcaneum, meaning heel; pl.: calcanei or calcanea) or heel bone is a bone of the tarsus of the foot which constitutes the heel. In humans, it attaches several muscles and the plantar fascia. In some animals, it is the point of the hock.

Capitate bone.description: The capitate bone, also known as os magnum, is a bone in the human wrist found in the center of the carpal bone region, located at the distal end of the radius and ulna bones. It articulates with the third metacarpal bone (the middle finger) and forms the third carpometacarpal joint. The capitate bone is the largest of the carpal bones in the human hand.

Cervical vertebrae.description: In tetrapods, cervical vertebrae (sg.: vertebra) are the vertebrae of the neck, immediately below the skull. Truncal vertebrae (divided into thoracic and lumbar vertebrae in mammals) lie caudal (toward the tail) of cervical vertebrae. In sauropsid species, the cervical vertebrae bear cervical ribs.

Chorda tympani.supplies:
Taste (anterior 2/3 of tongue)
Submandibular gland
Sublingual gland

Clavicle.description: The clavicle, collarbone, or keybone is a slender, S-shaped long bone approximately 15 cm long that serves as a strut between the shoulder blade and the sternum (breastbone). There are two clavicles, one on each side of the body. The clavicle is the only long bone in the body that lies horizontally. Together with the shoulder blade, it makes up the shoulder girdle.

Common fibular nerve.branches: Deep fibular nerve and superficial fibular nerve
Common fibular nerve.supplies: Anterior compartment of leg, lateral compartment of leg, extensor digitorum brevis

Common palmar digital nerves of ulnar ne.branches: proper palmar digital nerves of ulnar nerve

Coracobrachialis muscle.insertion: Anteromedial surface of humerus distal to crest of lesser tubercle
Coracobrachialis muscle.action: Adducts humerus, flexes the arm at glenohumeral joint

Cuboid bone.description: In the human body, the cuboid bone is one of the seven tarsal bones of the foot.

Cuneiform bones.description:
There are three cuneiform ("wedge-shaped") bones in the human foot:
the first or medial cuneiform
the second or intermediate cuneiform, also known as the middle cuneiform
the third or lateral cuneiform

Deep branch of ulnar nerve.supplies: dorsal interossei, palmar interossei, lumbricals #3 and 4, adductor pollicis, hypothenar eminence

Deltoid muscle.origin: The anterior border and upper surface of the lateral third of the clavicle, acromion, spine of the scapula
Deltoid muscle.blood: Thoracoacromial artery, anterior and posterior humeral circumflex artery

Depressor anguli oris muscle.nerve: Marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve

Depressor labii inferioris muscle.origin: Oblique line of the mandible, between the symphysis and the mental foramen
Depressor labii inferioris muscle.insertion: Integument of the lower lip, orbicularis oris fibers, its fellow of the opposite side
Depressor labii inferioris muscle.nerve: Marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve

Dorsal scapular nerve.supplies: Rhomboid minor, rhomboid major, levator scapulae

Ethmoid bone.description: The ethmoid bone (from Ancient Greek: ἡθμός) is an unpaired bone in the skull that separates the nasal cavity from the brain. It is located at the roof of the nose, between the two orbits. The cubical (cube-shaped) bone is lightweight due to a spongy construction. The ethmoid bone is one of the bones that make up the orbit of the eye.

Extensor carpi radialis brevis muscle.origin: Humerus at the anterior of lateral epicondyle (common extensor tendon)
Extensor carpi radialis brevis muscle.action: Extensor and abductor of the hand at the wrist joint
Extensor carpi radialis brevis muscle.nerve: Deep branch of the radial nerve

Extensor carpi radialis longus muscle.action: Extensor at the wrist joint, abducts the hand at the wrist

Extensor carpi ulnaris muscle.origin:
Humeral head: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus.
Ulnar head: Olecranon, posterior surface of ulna, antebrachial fascia

Extensor digiti minimi muscle.origin: The anterior portion of the lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor tendon)
Extensor digiti minimi muscle.insertion: At the extensor expansion, located at the base of the middle and distal phalanx of digit V on the dorsal side
Extensor digiti minimi muscle.action: Extends the wrist and the little finger at all joints

Extensor digitorum brevis muscle.insertion: Proximal dorsal region of middle phalanges 2, 3 and 4

Extensor digitorum longus muscle.origin: Anterior lateral condyle of tibia, anterior shaft of fibula and superior 3/4 of interosseous membrane
Extensor digitorum longus muscle.insertion: Dorsal surface; middle and distal phalanges of lateral four digits
Extensor digitorum longus muscle.action: Extension of toes and dorsiflexion of ankle

Extensor digitorum muscle.insertion: Extensor expansion of middle and distal phalanges of the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th fingers
Extensor digitorum muscle.action: Extension of hand, wrist and fingers

Extensor hallucis brevis muscle.insertion: Proximal phalanx of digit 1 (hallux, or the great toe)

Extensor hallucis longus muscle.origin: Arises from the middle portion of the fibula on the anterior surface and the interosseous membrane
Extensor hallucis longus muscle.insertion: Inserts on the dorsal side of the base of the distal phalanx of the big toe
Extensor hallucis longus muscle.action: Extends (raises) the big toe and assists in dorsiflexion of the foot at the ankle. Also is a weak evertor/invertor

Extensor indicis muscle.origin: Posterior distal third of ulna and interosseous membrane

Extensor pollicis brevis muscle.action: Extension of thumb at metacarpophalangeal joint

Extensor pollicis longus muscle.origin: Middle third of posterior surface of ulna, interosseous membrane
Extensor pollicis longus muscle.action: Extension of the thumb (metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal)
Extensor pollicis longus muscle.nerve: Posterior interosseous nerve (branching from the radial nerve)

External obturator muscle.nerve: Posterior branch of obturator nerve (third and fourth lumbar nerves)

Facial nerve.supplies:
Motor: Muscles of facial expression, posterior belly of digastric, stylohyoid, stapedius
Special sensory: taste to anterior two-thirds of tongue
Parasympathetic: submandibular gland, sublingual gland, lacrimal glands

Femur.description: The femur (pl.: femurs or femora), or thigh bone is the only bone in the thigh — the region of the lower limb between the hip and the knee. In many four-legged animals, the femur is the upper bone of the hindleg.
Femur.articulations:
Hip: acetabulum of pelvis superiorly
knee: with the tibia and patella inferiorly

Fibula.description: The fibula (pl.: fibulae or fibulas) or calf bone is a leg bone on the lateral side of the tibia, to which it is connected above and below. It is the smaller of the two bones and, in proportion to its length, the most slender of all the long bones. Its upper extremity is small, placed toward the back of the head of the tibia, below the knee joint and excluded from the formation of this joint.
Fibula.articulations:
Superior and inferior tibiofibular joint
Ankle

Fibularis longus.origin: Proximal part of lateral surface of shaft of fibula and head of fibula

Fibularis tertius.origin: Distal anterior surface of the fibula also the interosseous membrane
Fibularis tertius.action: Dorsiflexion and eversion of the foot

Fifth metacarpal bone.description: The fifth metacarpal bone (metacarpal bone of the little finger or pinky finger) is the most medial and second-shortest of the metacarpal bones.

Fifth metatarsal bone.description: The fifth metatarsal bone is a long bone in the foot, and is palpable along the distal outer edges of the feet. It is the second smallest of the five metatarsal bones. The fifth metatarsal is analogous to the fifth metacarpal bone in the hand.

First metacarpal bone.description: The first metacarpal bone or the metacarpal bone of the thumb is the first bone proximal to the thumb. It is connected to the trapezium of the carpus at the first carpometacarpal joint and to the proximal thumb phalanx at the first metacarpophalangeal joint.

First metatarsal bone.description: The first metatarsal bone is the bone in the foot just behind the big toe. The first metatarsal bone is the shortest of the metatarsal bones and by far the thickest and strongest of them.

Flexor carpi radialis muscle.origin: Medial epicondyle of humerus (common flexor tendon)
Flexor carpi radialis muscle.insertion: Bases of second and third metacarpal bones

Flexor carpi ulnaris muscle.origin: Medial epicondyle (common flexor tendon) and medial margin on olecranon of ulna
Flexor carpi ulnaris muscle.insertion: Pisiform, hook of the hamate, base of the fifth metacarpal bone (volar aspect)
Flexor carpi ulnaris muscle.nerve: Muscular branches of ulnar nerve (from C8 and T1)

Flexor digiti minimi brevis muscle of fo.insertion: First phalanx of the fifth toe
Flexor digiti minimi brevis muscle of fo.action: Flexion and adduction of the fifth toe
Flexor digiti minimi brevis muscle of fo.nerve: Superficial branch of lateral plantar nerve

Flexor digitorum brevis muscle.action: Flexion of the lateral four digits
Flexor digitorum brevis muscle.blood: Medial and lateral plantar arteries and plantar arch, plantar metatarsal and plantar digital arteries

Flexor digitorum longus muscle.origin: Posterior surface of the body of the tibia
Flexor digitorum longus muscle.insertion: Plantar surface; base of the distal phalanges of the four lesser toes
Flexor digitorum longus muscle.action: Flexion of the four smaller digits

Flexor digitorum profundus muscle.origin: Upper 3/4 of the anterior and medial surfaces of the body of the ulna, interosseous membrane and deep fascia of the forearm
Flexor digitorum profundus muscle.insertion: Base of the distal phalanges of the fingers
Flexor digitorum profundus muscle.action: Flex hand and both interphalangeal joints
Flexor digitorum profundus muscle.nerve: Lateral part of the muscle by median (anterior interosseous), medial (ulnar) part of the muscle by muscular branches of ulnar

Flexor digitorum superficialis muscle.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor tendon) as well as parts of the radius and ulna
Flexor digitorum superficialis muscle.insertion: Anterior margins on the base of the middle phalanges of the four fingers
Flexor digitorum superficialis muscle.action: Flexor of fingers (primarily at proximal interphalangeal joints)

Flexor hallucis brevis muscle.origin: Plantar aspect of the cuneiforms, plantar calcaneocuboid ligament, long plantar ligament
Flexor hallucis brevis muscle.insertion: Medial Head: Medial sesamoid bone of the metatarsophalangeal joint, proximal phalanx of great toe. Lateral head: Lateral sesamoid bone of the metatarsophalangeal joint, proximal phalanx of great toe

Flexor hallucis longus muscle.insertion: Plantar surface; base of distal phalanx of hallux
Flexor hallucis longus muscle.action: Flexes all joints of the big toe, plantar flexion of the ankle joint

Flexor pollicis longus muscle.origin: The middle 1/2 of the anterior surface of the radius and adjacent to the interosseus membrane.
Flexor pollicis longus muscle.insertion: The base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
Flexor pollicis longus muscle.nerve: Anterior interosseous nerve (branch of median nerve) (C8, T1)

Fourth metacarpal bone.description: The fourth metacarpal bone (metacarpal bone of the ring finger) is shorter and smaller than the third.

Fourth metatarsal bone.description: The fourth metatarsal bone is a long bone in the foot. It is smaller in size than the third metatarsal bone and is the third longest (and smallest) of the five metatarsal bones. The fourth metatarsal is analogous to the fourth metacarpal bone in the hand

Frontal bone.description: In the human skull, the frontal bone or sincipital bone is an unpaired bone which consists of two portions. These are the vertically oriented squamous part, and the horizontally oriented orbital part, making up the bony part of the forehead, part of the bony orbital cavity holding the eye, and part of the bony part of the nose respectively. The name comes from the Latin word frons (meaning "forehead").
Frontal bone.articulations: Twelve bones: the sphenoid, the ethmoid, the two parietals, the two nasals, the two maxillae, the two lacrimals, and the two zygomatics

Gastrocnemius muscle.origin: Proximal to articular surfaces of lateral condyle of femur and medial condyle of femur
Gastrocnemius muscle.insertion: Tendo calcaneus (Achilles tendon) into mid-posterior calcaneus
Gastrocnemius muscle.nerve: Tibial nerve from the sciatic, specifically, nerve roots S1–S2

Genitofemoral nerve.supplies:
Cremaster muscle
Anterior scrotum in males
Mons pubis in females

Glossopharyngeal nerve.supplies:
Motor: stylopharyngeus
Sensory: Oropharynx, Eustachian tube, middle ear, posterior third of tongue, carotid sinus, carotid body
Special sensory: Taste to posterior third of tongue

Gluteus maximus.origin: Gluteal surface of ilium, lumbar fascia, sacrum, sacrotuberous ligament
Gluteus maximus.insertion: Gluteal tuberosity of the femur and iliotibial tract
Gluteus maximus.action: External rotation and extension of the hip joint, supports the extended knee through the iliotibial tract, chief antigravity muscle in sitting and abduction of the hip
Gluteus maximus.nerve: Inferior gluteal nerve (L5, S1 and S2 nerve roots)

Gluteus medius.origin: Gluteal surface of ilium, under gluteus maximus, Aponeurosis glutea
Gluteus medius.action: Abduction of the hip; preventing adduction of the hip. Medial/internal rotation and flexion of the hip (anterior fibers). Extension and lateral/external rotation of the hip (posterior fibers)
Gluteus medius.nerve: Superior gluteal nerve (L4, L5, S1 nerve roots)

Gluteus minimus.origin: From area in between the anterior gluteal line and inferior gluteal line of gluteal surface ilium, under gluteus medius.
Gluteus minimus.action: Works in concert with gluteus medius: abduction of the hip; preventing adduction of the hip. Medial rotation of thigh.
Gluteus minimus.nerve: Superior gluteal nerve (L4, L5, S1 nerve roots)

Gracilis muscle.action: Flexes, medially rotates, and adducts the hip

Hamate bone.description: The hamate bone (from Latin hamatus, 'hooked'), or unciform bone (from Latin uncus, 'hook'), Latin os hamatum and occasionally abbreviated as just hamatum, is a bone in the human wrist readily distinguishable by its wedge shape and a hook-like process ("hamulus") projecting from its palmar surface.
Hamate bone.articulations:
Articulates with five bones:
the lunate proximally
the fourth and fifth metacarpals distally
the triquetrum medially
the capitate laterally

Hip bone.description: The hip bone (os coxae, innominate bone, or coxal bone) is a large flat bone, constricted in the center and expanded above and below. In some vertebrates (including humans before puberty) it is composed of three parts: the ilium, ischium, and the pubis.

Humerus.description: The humerus (pl.: humeri) is a long bone in the arm that runs from the shoulder to the elbow. It connects the scapula and the two bones of the lower arm, the radius and ulna, and consists of three sections. The humeral upper extremity consists of a rounded head, a narrow neck, and two short processes (tubercles, sometimes called tuberosities). The shaft is cylindrical in its upper portion, and more prismatic below.

Hypoglossal nerve.supplies: Genioglossus, hyoglossus, styloglossus, intrinsic muscles of the tongue

Iliacus muscle.origin: Upper two-thirds of the iliac fossa
Iliacus muscle.insertion: Base of the lesser trochanter of femur
Iliacus muscle.blood: Medial femoral circumflex artery, iliac branch of iliolumbar artery

Iliocostalis.origin: Sacrum, iliac crest, thoracolumbar fascia, spinous processes of vertebrae from T11 - L5
Iliocostalis.action: Unilaterally: laterally flex the vertebral column to the same side. Bilaterally: Extend the vertebral column.

Iliohypogastric nerve.supplies:
Sensory: Skin over the lateral gluteal region and above the pubis
Motor: internal oblique and transverse abdominal muscles

Ilioinguinal nerve.supplies: Skin over the root of the penis and upper part of the scrotum (male), skin covering the mons pubis and labium majus (female). Motor innervation of the transverse abdominus and obliques.

Inferior nasal concha.description: The inferior nasal concha (inferior turbinated bone or inferior turbinal/turbinate) is one of the three paired nasal conchae in the nose. It extends horizontally along the lateral wall of the nasal cavity and consists of a lamina of spongy bone, curled upon itself like a scroll, (turbinate meaning inverted cone). The inferior nasal conchae are considered a pair of facial bones.
Inferior nasal concha.articulations: Ethmoid, maxilla, lacrimal and palatine bone

Infraspinatus muscle.insertion: Middle facet of greater tubercle of the humerus
Infraspinatus muscle.action: External rotation of arm and stabilization of glenohumeral joint

Internal obturator muscle.insertion: Medial aspect of the greater trochanter
Internal obturator muscle.action: Abducts and laterally rotates the extended hip and abducts the flexed thigh at the hip, and stabilizes the hip during walking
Internal obturator muscle.nerve: Nerve to obturator internus (L5, S1, S2)

Lacrimal bone.description: The lacrimal bones are two small and fragile bones of the facial skeleton; in humans, they are roughly the size of the little fingernail and situated at the front part of the medial wall of the orbit. They each have two surfaces and four borders. Several bony landmarks of the lacrimal bones function in the process of lacrimation.

Lateral cutaneous nerve of thigh.supplies: Skin on the lateral part of the thigh

Lateral plantar nerve.supplies: Sole, abductor digiti minimi muscle (foot), flexor digiti minimi brevis muscle (foot), quadratus plantae, 3 lateral lumbricals of the foot, adductor hallucis muscle, plantar interossei muscles, dorsal interossei muscles

Lateral pterygoid muscle.origin: Superior head: infratemporal surface of sphenoid bone. Inferior head: lateral pterygoid plate
Lateral pterygoid muscle.insertion: Superior head: anterior side of the mandibular condyle. Inferior head: pterygoid fovea
Lateral pterygoid muscle.action: Depresses and protrudes mandible, side to side movement of mandible
Lateral pterygoid muscle.nerve: Lateral pterygoid nerve from mandibular nerve

Latissimus dorsi muscle.origin: Spinous processes of vertebrae T7-S5, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, inferior 4 ribs and inferior angle of scapula
Latissimus dorsi muscle.insertion: Floor of intertubercular groove of the humerus
Latissimus dorsi muscle.action: Adducts, extends and internally rotates the arm when the insertion is moved towards the origin. When observing the muscle action of the origin towards the insertion, the lats are a very powerful rotator of the trunk.
Latissimus dorsi muscle.blood: Thoracodorsal branch of the subscapular artery

Levator anguli oris.nerve: Buccal branches of the facial nerve

Levator labii superioris.insertion: Skin and muscle of the upper lip (labii superioris)
Levator labii superioris.nerve: Buccal branch of the facial nerve (C.N. VII)

Levator labii superioris alaeque nasi mu.action: Dilates the nostril; elevates the upper lip and wing of the nose

Levator scapulae muscle.origin: Posterior tubercles of transverse processes of C1 - C4 vertebrae
Levator scapulae muscle.insertion: Superior part of medial border of scapula
Levator scapulae muscle.action: Elevates scapula and tilts its glenoid cavity inferiorly by downwardly rotating the scapula
Levator scapulae muscle.nerve: Cervical nerve (C3, C4) and dorsal scapular nerve (C5)

Longissimus.action: Laterally: Flex the head and neck to the same side. Bilaterally: Extend the vertebral column.

Lumbar vertebrae.description: The lumbar vertebrae are located between the thoracic vertebrae and sacrum. They form the lower part of the back in humans, and the region of the spine between the rib cage and pelvis in quadrupedal mammals. In humans, there are typically five lumbar vertebrae.

Lumbricals of the foot.origin: Medial borders of long flexor tendons
Lumbricals of the foot.insertion: Proximal phalanges and extensor tendons of the 4 lateral toes
Lumbricals of the foot.action: Flexes metatarsophalangeal joints, extends interphalangeal joints

Lunate bone.description: The lunate bone (semilunar bone) is a carpal bone in the human hand. It is distinguished by its deep concavity and crescentic outline. It is situated in the center of the proximal row carpal bones, which lie between the ulna and radius and the hand. The lunate carpal bone is situated between the lateral scaphoid bone and medial triquetral bone.
Lunate bone.articulations:
Radius proximally
capitate and hamate distally
scaphoid laterally
triquetrum medially
triangular fibrocartilage

Mandible.description: In jawed vertebrates, the mandible (from the Latin mandibula, 'for chewing'), lower jaw, or jawbone is a bone that makes up the lower – and typically more mobile – component of the mouth (the upper jaw being known as the maxilla).

Masseter muscle.origin: Zygomatic arch and maxillary process of zygomatic bone
Masseter muscle.insertion: Angle surface of ramus of mandible, coronoid process
Masseter muscle.action: Elevation (as in closing of the mouth) and protrusion of mandible

Maxilla.description: In vertebrates, the maxilla (pl.: maxillae) is the upper fixed (not fixed in Neopterygii) bone of the jaw formed from the fusion of two maxillary bones. In humans, the upper jaw includes the hard palate in the front of the mouth. The two maxillary bones are fused at the intermaxillary suture, forming the anterior nasal spine.

Maxillary nerve.branches: Infraorbital nerve, zygomatic nerve, palatine nerve, nasopalatine nerve, sphenopalatine ganglion

Medial plantar nerve.supplies:
Sole
abductor hallucis muscle
flexor digitorum brevis muscle
flexor hallucis brevis muscle
1 medial lumbrical

Medial pterygoid muscle.origin:
Deep head: medial side of lateral pterygoid plate behind the upper teeth
Superficial head: pyramidal process of palatine bone and maxillary tuberosity
Medial pterygoid muscle.action: Elevates mandible, closes jaw, helps lateral pterygoids in moving the jaw from side to side
Medial pterygoid muscle.nerve: Mandibular nerve via nerve to medial pterygoid

Median nerve.supplies: Anterior compartment of the forearm (with two exceptions), thenar eminence, lumbricals, skin of the hand

Mentalis.action: Elevates and wrinkles skin of chin, protrudes lower lip

Multifidus muscle.origin: Sacrum, erector spinae aponeurosis, PSIS, and iliac crest
Multifidus muscle.action: Provides proprioceptive feedback and input due to high muscle spindle density; Bilateral backward extension, unilateral ipsilateral side-bending and contralateral rotation.

Muscular branches of the radial nerve.supplies: Posterior compartment of the arm, mobile wad

Muscular branches of ulnar nerve.supplies: Flexor carpi ulnaris, Flexor digitorum profundus

Mylohyoid nerve.supplies: Mylohyoid muscle, anterior belly of digastric muscle

Nasal bone.description: The nasal bones are two small oblong bones, varying in size and form in different individuals; they are placed side by side at the middle and upper part of the face and by their junction, form the bridge of the upper one third of the nose.

Nasalis muscle.action: Compresses bridge of nose, depresses tip of nose, elevates corners of nostrils
Nasalis muscle.nerve: Buccal branch of the facial nerve

Navicular bone.description: The navicular bone is a small bone found in the feet of most mammals.

Nerve to quadratus femoris.supplies: Quadratus femoris muscle, inferior gemellus muscle

Obturator nerve.branches: Posterior branch of obturator nerve, anterior branch of obturator nerve

Occipital bone.description: The occipital bone is a cranial dermal bone and the main bone of the occiput (back and lower part of the skull). It is trapezoidal in shape and curved on itself like a shallow dish. The occipital bone lies over the occipital lobes of the cerebrum. At the base of the skull in the occipital bone, there is a large oval opening called the foramen magnum, which allows the passage of the spinal cord.
Occipital bone.articulations: The two parietals, the two temporals, the sphenoid, and the atlas

Occipitalis muscle.origin: Superior nuchal line of the occipital bone and mastoid process of the temporal bone
Occipitalis muscle.nerve: Posterior auricular nerve (a branch of the facial nerve)

Oculomotor nerve.supplies: Superior rectus, inferior rectus, medial rectus, inferior oblique, levator palpebrae superioris, sphincter pupillae (parasympathetics), ciliaris muscle (parasympathetics)

Ophthalmic nerve.branches: Frontal nerve, lacrimal nerve, nasociliary nerve

Orbicularis oculi muscle.origin: Frontal bone; medial palpebral ligament; lacrimal bone
Orbicularis oculi muscle.nerve: Temporal (orbital, palpebral) and zygomatic (lacrimal) branches of facial nerve

Orbicularis oris muscle.action: It is sometimes known as the kissing muscle because it is used to pucker the lips.
Orbicularis oris muscle.blood: Inferior labial artery and superior labial artery.

Palatine bone.description: In anatomy, the palatine bones (derived from the Latin palatum) are two irregular bones of the facial skeleton in many animal species, located above the uvula in the throat. Together with the maxilla, they comprise the hard palate.

Palmaris longus muscle.origin: Medial epicondyle of humerus (common flexor tendon)
Palmaris longus muscle.insertion: Palmar aponeurosis and flexor retinaculum of the hand

Parietal bone.description: The parietal bones are two bones in the skull which, when joined at a fibrous joint known as a cranial suture, form the sides and roof of the neurocranium. In humans, each bone is roughly quadrilateral in form, and has two surfaces, four borders, and four angles. It is named from the Latin paries (-ietis), wall.
Parietal bone.articulations: Five bones: the opposite parietal, the occipital, the frontal, the temporal, and the sphenoid

Patella.description: The patella (pl.: patellae or patellas), also known as the kneecap, is a flat, rounded triangular bone which articulates with the femur (thigh bone) and covers and protects the anterior articular surface of the knee joint. The patella is found in many tetrapods, such as mice, cats, birds, humans, and dogs, but not in whales, or most reptiles.

Pectineus muscle.origin: Pectineal line of the pubic bone

Pectoralis major.origin:
Clavicular head: anterior surface of the medial half of the clavicle.
Sternocostal head: anterior surface of the sternum, the superior six costal cartilages, and the aponeurosis of the external oblique muscle
Pectoralis major.insertion:
Lateral lip of the bicipital groove of the humerus
(anteromedial proximal humerus)
Pectoralis major.action:
Clavicular head: flexes the humerus
Sternocostal head: horizontal and vertical adduction, extension, and internal rotation of the humerus
Depression and abduction of the scapula.
Pectoralis major.nerve:
Lateral pectoral nerve and medial pectoral nerve
Clavicular head: C5 and C6
Sternocostal head: C7, C8 and T1
Pectoralis major.blood: Pectoral branch of the thoracoacromial trunk

Pectoralis minor.origin: Third to fifth ribs, near the costochondral junction
Pectoralis minor.insertion: Medial border and superior surface of the coracoid process of the scapula
Pectoralis minor.action: Stabilizes the scapula by drawing it inferiorly and anteriorly against the thoracic wall, raises ribs in inhalation
Pectoralis minor.blood: Pectoral branch of the thoracoacromial trunk

Phalanx bone.description: The phalanges (sg.: phalanx) are digital bones in the hands and feet of most vertebrates. In primates, the thumbs and big toes have two phalanges each, while the other digits have three phalanges each. The phalanges are classed as long bones.

Piriformis muscle.nerve: Nerve to the piriformis (L5, S1, and S2)
Piriformis muscle.blood: Inferior gluteal, lateral sacral and superior gluteal artery

Pisiform bone.description: The pisiform bone, also spelled pisiforme (from the Latin pisiformis, pea-shaped), is a small knobbly, sesamoid bone that is found in the wrist. It forms the ulnar border of the carpal tunnel.

Plantar interossei muscles.insertion: Medial side of proximal phalanges of 3rd to 5th toe
Plantar interossei muscles.blood: Plantar artery, and dorsal metatarsal A

Plantaris muscle.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of femur above lateral head of gastrocnemius
Plantaris muscle.insertion: Tendo calcaneus (medial side, deep to gastrocnemius tendon)
Plantaris muscle.action: Plantar flexes foot and flexes knee
Plantaris muscle.nerve: Tibial nerve from anterior rami of S1-S2

Popliteus muscle.insertion: Posterior surface of the tibia proximal to the soleus line
Popliteus muscle.action: Medially rotates tibia on the femur if the femur is fixed (sitting down) or laterally rotates femur on the tibia if tibia is fixed (standing up), unlocks the knee to allow flexion (bending), helps to prevent the forward dislocation of the femur while crouching

Posterior cord.from: Brachial plexus - posterior divisions of the three trunks
Posterior cord.branches:
Subscapular, up. and low.
thoracodorsal
axillary
radial

Posterior interosseous nerve.from: Deep branch of the radial nerve
Posterior interosseous nerve.supplies:
Extensor carpi radialis brevis
Extensor digitorum
Extensor digiti minimi
Extensor carpi ulnaris
Supinator muscle
Abductor pollicis longus
Extensor pollicis brevis
Extensor pollicis longus
Extensor indicis

Procerus muscle.origin: From fascia over the lower part of the nasal bone
Procerus muscle.insertion: Into the skin of the lower part of the forehead between the eyebrows
Procerus muscle.action: Draws down the medial angle of the eyebrow giving expressions of frowning
Procerus muscle.nerve: Temporal branch of the facial nerve

Pronator quadratus muscle.origin: Medial, anterior surface of the ulna
Pronator quadratus muscle.insertion: Lateral, anterior surface of the radius

Pronator teres muscle.origin:
Humeral head: medial supracondylar ridge of humerus slightly above the medial epicondyle of humerus (common flexor tendon)
Ulnar head: coronoid process of ulna
Pronator teres muscle.insertion: Middle of the lateral surface of the body of the radius

Proper palmar digital nerves of median n.from: Common palmar digital nerves of median nerve

Proper palmar digital nerves of ulnar ne.from: Common palmar digital nerves of ulnar nerve

Psoas major muscle.origin: Transverse processes of T12–L4 and the lateral aspects of the discs between them
Psoas major muscle.insertion: In the lesser trochanter of the femur
Psoas major muscle.nerve: Lumbar plexus via anterior branches of L1–L3 nerves

Pudendal nerve.branches:
Inferior rectal nerves
perineal nerve
dorsal nerve of the penis
dorsal nerve of the clitoris

Quadratus femoris muscle.action: Lateral rotation and adduction of thigh
Quadratus femoris muscle.blood:
Inferior gluteal artery
medial circumflex femoral artery

Quadratus lumborum muscle.insertion: Inferior border of 12th rib and L1-L4
Quadratus lumborum muscle.action: Alone (unilateral), lateral flexion of vertebral column; Together (bilateral), depression of thoracic rib cage
Quadratus lumborum muscle.nerve: The twelfth thoracic and first through fourth ventral rami of lumbar nerves (T12, L1-L4)
Quadratus lumborum muscle.blood: Lumbar arteries, lumbar branch of iliolumbar artery

Quadratus plantae muscle.action: Assists flexor digitorum longus in flexion of DIP joints

Radial nerve.supplies: Posterior compartment of the arm, posterior compartment of the forearm

Radius (bone).description: The radius or radial bone (pl.: radii or radiuses) is one of the two large bones of the forearm, the other being the ulna. It extends from the lateral side of the elbow to the thumb side of the wrist and runs parallel to the ulna. The ulna is longer than the radius, but the radius is thicker. The radius is a long bone, prism-shaped and slightly curved longitudinally.

Rectus abdominis muscle.insertion: Costal cartilages of ribs 5-7 xiphoid process of sternum
Rectus abdominis muscle.nerve: Segmentally by thoraco-abdominal nerves (T7 to T11) and subcostal (T12)

Rectus femoris muscle.origin: Anterior inferior iliac spine and the exterior surface of the bony ridge which forms the groove on the iliac portion of the acetabulum
Rectus femoris muscle.insertion: Inserts into the patellar tendon as one of the four quadriceps muscles
Rectus femoris muscle.blood: Descending branch of the lateral femoral circumflex artery

Rhomboid major muscle.origin: Spinous processes of the T2 to T5 vertebrae
Rhomboid major muscle.insertion: Medial border of the scapula, inferior to the insertion of rhomboid minor muscle
Rhomboid major muscle.action: Retracts the scapula and rotates it to depress the glenoid cavity. It also fixes the scapula to the thoracic wall.

Rhomboid minor muscle.origin: Nuchal ligaments and spinous processes of C7-T1
Rhomboid minor muscle.insertion: Medial border of scapula, superior to the insertion of rhomboid major muscle
Rhomboid minor muscle.action: Retracts and rotates scapula, fixes scapula to thoracic wall
Rhomboid minor muscle.blood: Deep branch of transverse cervical artery

Rib.description: In vertebrate anatomy, ribs (Latin: costae) are the long curved bones which form the rib cage, part of the axial skeleton. In most tetrapods, ribs surround the thoracic cavity, enabling the lungs to expand and thus facilitate breathing by expanding the thoracic cavity. They serve to protect the lungs, heart, and other vital organs of the thorax.

Risorius.nerve: Buccal branch of the facial nerve

Sacrum.description: The sacrum (pl.: sacra or sacrums), in human anatomy, is a triangular bone at the base of the spine that forms by the fusing of the sacral vertebrae (S1–S5) between ages 18 and 30.

Sartorius muscle.origin: Anterior superior iliac spine of the pelvic bone
Sartorius muscle.insertion: Anteromedial surface of the proximal tibia in the pes anserinus
Sartorius muscle.action: Flexion, abduction, and lateral rotation of the hip, flexion of the knee
Sartorius muscle.nerve: Femoral nerve (sometimes from the intermediate cutaneous nerve of thigh)

Scalene muscles.action: Elevation of first and second ribs
Scalene muscles.blood:
Ascending cervical artery
(branch of Inferior thyroid artery)

Scaphoid bone.description: The scaphoid bone is one of the carpal bones of the wrist. It is situated between the hand and forearm on the thumb side of the wrist (also called the lateral or radial side). It forms the radial border of the carpal tunnel. The scaphoid bone is the largest bone of the proximal row of wrist bones, its long axis being from above downward, lateralward, and forward.
Scaphoid bone.articulations:
Articulates with five bones
radius proximally
trapezoid bone and trapezium bone distally
capitate and lunate medially

Scapula.description: The scapula (pl.: scapulae or scapulas), also known as the shoulder blade, is the bone that connects the humerus (upper arm bone) with the clavicle (collar bone). Like their connected bones, the scapulae are paired, with each scapula on either side of the body being roughly a mirror image of the other. The name derives from the Classical Latin word for trowel or small shovel, which it was thought to resemble.

Sciatic nerve.supplies: Lateral rotator group (except piriformis and quadratus femoris) and the posterior compartment of thigh

Second metacarpal bone.description: The second metacarpal bone (metacarpal bone of the index finger) is the longest, and its base the largest, of all the metacarpal bones.

Second metatarsal bone.description: The second metatarsal bone is a long bone in the foot. It is the longest of the metatarsal bones, being prolonged backward and held firmly into the recess formed by the three cuneiform bones. The second metatarsal forms joints with the second proximal phalanx (a bone in the second toe) through the metatarsophalangeal joint, the cuneiform bones, third metatarsal and occasionally the first metatarsal bone.

Semimembranosus muscle.action: Extension of hip and flexion of knee
Semimembranosus muscle.nerve:
Tibial part of sciatic nerve
(L5, S1 and S2)

Semitendinosus muscle.origin: Lower quadrangular part of tuberosity of the ischium
Semitendinosus muscle.action: Flexion of knee, extension of the hip joint

Serratus anterior muscle.origin: Fleshy slips from the outer surface of upper from 1st to 9 ribs
Serratus anterior muscle.insertion: Costal aspect of medial margin of the scapula
Serratus anterior muscle.action: Protracts and stabilizes scapula, assists in upward rotation, assists in inspiration (when shoulder girdle is fixed)
Serratus anterior muscle.nerve: Long thoracic nerve (from roots of brachial plexus C5-C7)
Serratus anterior muscle.blood: Lateral thoracic artery, superior thoracic artery (upper part), thoracodorsal artery (lower part)

Serratus posterior inferior muscle.origin: Vertebrae: Spinous processes of T11 - L2
Serratus posterior inferior muscle.insertion: The inferior borders of the 9th through 12th ribs
Serratus posterior inferior muscle.action: Depress the lower ribs 9-12, aiding in expiration

Serratus posterior superior muscle.origin: Nuchal ligament (or ligamentum nuchae) and the spinous processes of the vertebrae C7 through T3
Serratus posterior superior muscle.insertion: The upper borders of the 2nd through 5th ribs

Soleus muscle.origin: Fibula, medial border of tibia (soleal line)
Soleus muscle.nerve: Tibial nerve, specifically, nerve roots L5–S2
Soleus muscle.blood: Popliteal artery, posterior tibial artery, peroneal artery

Sphenoid bone.description: The sphenoid bone is an unpaired bone of the neurocranium in mammals. It is situated in the middle of the skull towards the front, in front of the basilar part of the occipital bone. The sphenoid bone is one of the seven bones that articulate to form the orbit. The name originates from the Ancient Greek word sphekodes (σφηκώδης), meaning 'wasp-like', presumably referring to the bone's winged appearance.

Spinalis.origin:
Thoracis: Spinous process of upper lumbar and lower thoracic vertebrae.
Cervicis: nuchal ligament and spinous process of C7.
Spinalis.insertion:
Thoracis: Spinous process of upper thoracic vertebrae.
Cervicis: Spinous process of cervical vertebrae except atlas.
Spinalis.action: Laterally: Flex the head and neck to the same side. Bilaterally: Extend the vertebral column.

Splenius capitis muscle.origin: Nuchal ligament and spinous process of C7-T3
Splenius capitis muscle.insertion: Mastoid process of temporal and occipital bone
Splenius capitis muscle.action: Extend, rotate, and laterally flex the head
Splenius capitis muscle.nerve: Posterior ramus of spinal nerves C3 and C4

Splenius cervicis muscle.action: Bilaterally: Extend the head and neck, Unilaterally: Lateral flexion to the same side, Rotation to the same side.
Splenius cervicis muscle.nerve: Posterior rami of the lower Cervical spinal nerves
Splenius cervicis muscle.blood: Transverse cervical artery and occipital artery

Sternocleidomastoid muscle.origin: Manubrium and medial portion of the clavicle
Sternocleidomastoid muscle.insertion: Mastoid process of the temporal bone, superior nuchal line
Sternocleidomastoid muscle.action:
Unilaterally: contralateral cervical rotation, ipsilateral cervical flexion
Bilaterally: cervical flexion, elevation of sternum and assists in forced inhalation.
Sternocleidomastoid muscle.nerve:
Motor: spinal accessory nerve
sensory: cervical plexus
Proprioceptive: ventral primary rami of C2 and C3
Sternocleidomastoid muscle.blood: Occipital artery and the superior thyroid artery

Sternum.description: The sternum (pl.: sternums or sterna) or breastbone is a long flat bone located in the central part of the chest. It connects to the ribs via cartilage and forms the front of the rib cage, thus helping to protect the heart, lungs, and major blood vessels from injury. Shaped roughly like a necktie, it is one of the largest and longest flat bones of the body.

Subclavius muscle.insertion: Subclavian groove of clavicle (inferior surface of middle one third of the clavicle)
Subclavius muscle.action:
Depression of clavicle
elevation of first rib

Subscapularis muscle.action: Internally rotates and adducts humerus; stabilizes shoulder
Subscapularis muscle.nerve: Upper subscapular nerve, lower subscapular nerve (C5, C6)

Superficial fibular nerve.branches: Medial dorsal cutaneous nerve, intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve

Superior gluteal nerve.supplies: Gluteus medius, gluteus minimus, tensor fasciæ latæ

Supinator muscle.origin: Lateral epicondyle of humerus, supinator crest of ulna, radial collateral ligament, annular ligament
Supinator muscle.nerve: Deep branch of the radial nerve

Supraspinatus muscle.insertion: Superior facet of greater tubercle of humerus
Supraspinatus muscle.action: Abduction of arm and stabilizes humerus

Sural nerve.from: Union of Medial sural cutaneous nerve + sural communicating nerve
Sural nerve.branches: Sural nerve forms after piercing out of deep fascia or after an anastomosis, terminates as lateral dorsal cutaneous nerve
Sural nerve.supplies: Supplies cutaneous sensation to the skin of the posterolateral leg and lateral ankle.

Talus bone.description: The talus (Latin for ankle or ankle bone; pl.: tali), talus bone, astragalus, or ankle bone is one of the group of foot bones known as the tarsus. The tarsus forms the lower part of the ankle joint. It transmits the entire weight of the body from the lower legs to the foot.

Temporal bone.description: The temporal bone is a paired bone situated at the sides and base of the skull, lateral to the temporal lobe of the cerebral cortex.
Temporal bone.articulations: Occipital, parietal, sphenoid, mandible and zygomatic

Temporalis muscle.origin: Temporal lines on the parietal bone of the skull and the superior temporal surface of the sphenoid bone
Temporalis muscle.insertion: Coronoid process of the mandible and retromolar fossa
Temporalis muscle.nerve: Deep temporal nerves, branches of the anterior division of the mandibular nerve (V3)

Temporoparietalis muscle.nerve: Temporal branches of the facial nerve

Tensor fasciae latae muscle.action: Hip - flexion, medial rotation, abduction, knee - lateral rotation, torso - stabilization
Tensor fasciae latae muscle.blood: Primarily lateral circumflex femoral artery, superior gluteal artery

Teres major muscle.origin: Posterior aspect of the inferior angle of the scapula
Teres major muscle.insertion: Medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus
Teres major muscle.action: Adduct the humerus, internal rotation (medial rotation) of the humerus, extend the humerus from flexed position
Teres major muscle.nerve: Lower subscapular nerve (segmental levels C5 and C6)

Teres minor muscle.insertion: Inferior facet of greater tubercle of the humerus
Teres minor muscle.action: Laterally rotates the arm, stabilizes humerus
Teres minor muscle.blood: Posterior circumflex humeral artery and the circumflex scapular artery

Third metacarpal bone.description: The third metacarpal bone (metacarpal bone of the middle finger) is a little smaller than the second.

Third metatarsal bone.description: The third metatarsal bone is a long bone in the foot. It is the second longest metatarsal, the longest being the second metatarsal. The third metatarsal is analogous to the third metacarpal bone in the hand

Thoracic vertebrae.description: In vertebrates, thoracic vertebrae compose the middle segment of the vertebral column, between the cervical vertebrae and the lumbar vertebrae. In humans, there are twelve thoracic vertebrae of intermediate size between the cervical and lumbar vertebrae; they increase in size going towards the lumbar vertebrae.

Tibia.description: The tibia (pl.: tibiae or tibias), also known as the shinbone, shankbone or simply the shin, is the larger, stronger, and anterior (frontal) of the two bones in the leg below the knee in vertebrates (the other being the fibula, behind and to the outside of the tibia); it connects the knee with the ankle. The tibia is found on the medial side of the leg next to the fibula and closer to the median plane.
Tibia.articulations:
Knee, ankle, superior and
inferior tibiofibular joint

Tibial nerve.branches: Medial plantar nerve, lateral plantar nerve
Tibial nerve.supplies:
Origin: Flexor digitorum longus, flexor hallucis longus
Anterior: semimembranosus, semitendinosus, long head of biceps femoris
Medial: abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis, flexor hallucis brevis, first lumbrical
Lateral: quadratus plantae, flexor digiti minimi, adductor hallucis, the interossei, three lumbricals and abductor digiti minimi

Tibialis anterior muscle.origin: From the upper 1/2 or 2/3 of the lateral surface of the tibia and the adjacent interosseous membrane
Tibialis anterior muscle.insertion: Medial cuneiform and the base of first metatarsal bone of the foot
Tibialis anterior muscle.action: Dorsiflexion and inversion of the foot

Tibialis posterior muscle.action: Inversion of the foot and plantar flexion of the foot at the ankle

Transverse abdominal muscle.origin: Iliac crest, inguinal ligament, thoracolumbar fascia, and costal cartilages 7-12
Transverse abdominal muscle.insertion: Xiphoid process, linea alba, pubic crest and pecten pubis via conjoint tendon
Transverse abdominal muscle.action: Compresses abdominal contents (bilateral), rotates trunk ipsilaterally (unilateral)
Transverse abdominal muscle.nerve: Thoracoabdominal nn. (T6-T11), Subcostal n. (T12), iliohypogastric nerve (L1), and ilioinguinal nerve (L1)

Trapezium (bone).description: The trapezium bone (greater multangular bone) is a carpal bone in the hand. It forms the radial border of the carpal tunnel.
Trapezium (bone).articulations:
1st metacarpal distally
scaphoid proximally
trapezoid medially
2nd metacarpal medially

Trapezius.origin: Medial one-third of superior nuchal line, external occipital protuberance, spinous processes of vertebrae C7-T12, Nuchal ligament
Trapezius.insertion: Posterior border of the lateral one-third of the clavicle, acromion process, and spine of scapula
Trapezius.action: Rotation, retraction, elevation, and depression of scapula
Trapezius.nerve:
Accessory nerve (motor)
cervical spinal nerves C3 and C4 (motor and sensation)
Trapezius.blood: Superficial branch of transverse cervical artery or superficial cervical artery

Trapezoid bone.description: The trapezoid bone (lesser multangular bone) is a carpal bone in tetrapods, including humans. It is the smallest bone in the distal row of carpal bones that give structure to the palm of the hand. It may be known by its wedge-shaped form, the broad end of the wedge constituting the dorsal, the narrow end the palmar surface; and by its having four articular facets touching each other, and separated by sharp edges.
Trapezoid bone.articulations:
Articulates with four bones:
scaphoid proximally
second metacarpal distally
trapezium bone laterally
capitate medially

Triceps.origin:
Long head: infraglenoid tubercle of scapula
Lateral head: above the radial groove
Medial head: below the radial groove
Triceps.action: Extends forearm, long head extends, adducts arm, extends shoulder
Triceps.blood: Deep brachial artery, posterior circumflex humeral artery (long head only)

Trigeminal nerve.branches:
Ophthalmic nerve
Maxillary nerve
Mandibular nerve
Trigeminal nerve.supplies:
Motor: Muscles of mastication, tensor tympani, tensor veli palatini, mylohyoid, anterior belly of the digastric
Sensory: Face, mouth, temporomandibular joint

Triquetral bone.description: The triquetral bone (also called triquetrum, pyramidal, three-faced, and formerly cuneiform bone) is located in the wrist on the medial side of the proximal row of the carpus between the lunate and pisiform bones. It is on the ulnar side of the hand, but does not directly articulate with the ulna.
Triquetral bone.articulations:
Articulates with three bones:
lunate laterally
pisiform in front
hamate distally
triangular articular disk which separates it from the lower end of the ulna.

Ulna.description: The ulna or ulnar bone (pl.: ulnae or ulnas) is a long bone in the forearm stretching from the elbow to the wrist. It is on the same side of the forearm as the little finger, running parallel to the radius, the forearm's other long bone. Longer and thinner than the radius, the ulna is considered to be the smaller long bone of the lower arm. The corresponding bone in the lower leg is the fibula.

Ulnar nerve.supplies:
Flexor carpi ulnaris
flexor digitorum profundus
lumbrical muscles
opponens digiti minimi
flexor digiti minimi
abductor digiti minimi
interossei
adductor pollicis

Upper trunk.from: Ventral rami of C5 and C6
Upper trunk.branches: Anterior division of upper trunk, posterior division of upper trunk, subclavian nerve, suprascapular nerve

Vastus lateralis muscle.origin: Greater trochanter, intertrochanteric line, and linea aspera of the femur
Vastus lateralis muscle.insertion: Patella by the quadriceps tendon and tibial tuberosity by the patellar ligament

Vomer.description: The vomer (Latin: vomer) is one of the unpaired facial bones of the skull. It is located in the midsagittal line, and articulates with the sphenoid, the ethmoid, the left and right palatine bones, and the left and right maxillary bones. The vomer forms the inferior part of the nasal septum in humans, with the superior part formed by the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid bone.

Xiphoid process.description: The xiphoid process, also referred to as the ensiform process, xiphisternum, or metasternum, constitutes a small cartilaginous process (extension) located in the inferior segment of the sternum, typically ossified in adult humans. Both the Greek-derived term xiphoid and its Latin equivalent, ensiform, connote a "swordlike" or "sword-shaped" morphology.

Zygomatic bone.description: In the human skull, the zygomatic bone (from Ancient Greek: ζῠγόν), also called cheekbone or malar bone, is a paired irregular bone, situated at the upper and lateral part of the face and forming part of the lateral wall and floor of the orbit, of the temporal fossa and the infratemporal fossa.
Zygomatic bone.articulations: Maxilla, temporal bone, sphenoid bone and frontal bone

Zygomaticus major muscle.action: Draws the angle of the mouth upward laterally
Zygomaticus major muscle.nerve: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial nerve

muscle.abductor digiti minimi of foot: Abductor digiti minimi muscle of foot
muscle.flexor digiti minimi brevis of foot: Flexor digiti minimi brevis muscle of foot
muscle.levator labii superioris alaeque nasi: Levator labii superioris alaeque nasi muscle

nerve.anterior cutaneous branches of femoral n: Anterior cutaneous branches of the femoral nerve
nerve.common palmar digital branches of median: Common palmar digital nerves of median nerve
nerve.common palmar digital branches of ulnar: Common palmar digital nerves of ulnar nerve
nerve.common plantar digital branches of later: Common plantar digital nerves of lateral plantar nerve
nerve.common plantar digital branches of media: Common plantar digital nerves of medial plantar nerve
nerve.dorsal digital branches of radial nerve: Dorsal digital nerves of radial nerve
nerve.dorsal digital branches of ulnar nerve: Dorsal digital nerves of ulnar nerve
nerve.inferior lateral brachial cutaneous nerv: Inferior lateral cutaneous nerve of arm
nerve.muscular branches of radial nerve: Muscular branches of the radial nerve
nerve.palmar branch of median nerve: Palmar branch of the median nerve
nerve.proper palmar digital branches of median: Proper palmar digital nerves of median nerve
nerve.proper palmar digital branches of ulnar: Proper palmar digital nerves of ulnar nerve
nerve.proper plantar digital branches of later: Proper plantar digital nerves of lateral plantar nerve
nerve.proper plantar digital branches of media: Proper plantar digital nerves of medial plantar nerve
nerve.superior lateral brachial cutaneous nerv: Superior lateral cutaneous nerve of arm
nerve.sural communicating branch of common fib: Sural communicating branch of common peroneal nerve
